data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is driven by the elimination of evapotranspiration and latent heat loss in cities, and the cross-city intensity gap is more pronounced in arid climates where rural vegetation is stressed but irrigated urban green spaces invert this dynamic.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If urban irrigation completely saturates the surface energy balance, the city may cool faster than dry rural land, inverting the UHI.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If frequent rainfall saturates both environments equally, the latent heat disparity vanishes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Impervious urban surfaces shed water, eliminating the latent heat sink of evapotranspiration and forcing all cooling into sensible heat flux. After sunset, rural areas cool rapidly as vegetation transpires, while cities remain hot.
